To restrict the activation to only include orders from the last 30 days, a filter on the Purchase Order Date must be added within the related attribute configuration in the activation itself.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (data graphs containing only 30 days of data) — data graphs are not relevant to activation related-attribute output.
Option B (data space filter to exclude older orders) — data space filters operate at the data visibility level, not activation attribute filtering.
Option D (SQL in Marketing Cloud Engagement) — a post-activation workaround that leaves the activation itself sending the wrong orders.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_considerations_for_related_attributes.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A consultant wants to confirm the Identity resolution they just set up. Which two features can the consultant use to validate the data on a unified profile? (Choose 2).
optionA: Identity Resolution
optionB: Data Actions
optionC: Data Explorer
optionD: Query API
explanation:
Data Explorer and the Query API are the two keyed features. Data Explorer lets you inspect the rows of any DLO or DMO, including the Unified Individual, to confirm that source records merged as expected (C), and the Query API returns unified profile data programmatically so field values and linkages can be verified outside the UI (D). Option A is the weak part of this item rather than a clean distractor: Identity Resolution does carry a validation surface of its own — the Resolution Summary reports match and reconciliation statistics after each ruleset run, and this deck keys exactly that as a valid way to validate a unified profile elsewhere. Treat C and D as the answer because they inspect the resulting data directly, but do not take from this item that identity resolution offers nothing to check.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Identity Resolution) — not simply wrong: the Resolution Summary is a documented validation surface. It is excluded here only because C and D inspect the resulting profile data directly, and the item is defective on this point.
Option B (Data Actions) — publish events downstream and are not an inspection surface.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_data_explorer.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_resolution_summary.htm&language=en_US&type=5

The Resolution Summary is a documented way to validate identity resolution output, so option A is not simply wrong, and this deck's own question on the same topic keys Identity Resolution as a validation feature. Key kept as the two that inspect profile data directly.

question:
When creating a segment on an individual, what is the result of using two separate containers linked by an AND as shown below?
GoodsProduct | Count | At Least | 1 / Color | Is Equal To | red
AND
GoodsProduct | Count | At Least | 1 / PrimaryProductCategory | Is Equal To | shoes
optionA: Individuals who purchased at least one of any red product and also purchased at least one pair of shoes
optionB: Individuals who purchased at least one red shoes as a single line item in a purchase
optionC: Individuals who made a purchase of at least one red shoes and nothing else
optionD: Individuals who purchased at least one of any red product or purchased at least one pair of shoes
explanation:
Individuals who purchased at least one of any red product and also purchased at least one pair of shoes is the result. Attributes placed in the same container act on the same data row of the container's object; attributes placed in separate containers are evaluated independently of each other. Salesforce's own worked example is this question: put yellow in one container and scarf in another, and the query engine looks for customers who purchased any yellow product and purchased a scarf of any color — not a yellow scarf. So two containers joined by AND return individuals who bought at least one red product and, separately, at least one pair of shoes.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (at least one red shoes as a single line item) — that is what you would get by putting Color and PrimaryProductCategory in the same container; separate containers do not require both on one row.
Option C (at least one red shoes and nothing else) — adds an exclusivity the filter never expresses.
Option D (any red product or any pair of shoes) — OR logic; the containers are joined by AND.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.c360_a_container_basics.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A consultant is helping a beauty company ingest its profile data into Data Cloud. The company's source data includes several fields, such as eye color, skin type, and hair color, that are not fields in the standard Individual data model object (DMO). What should the consultant recommend to map this data to be used for both segmentation and identity resolution?
optionA: Create a custom DMO from scratch that has all fields that are needed
optionB: Create a custom DMO with only the additional fields and map it to the standard Individual DMO
optionC: Create custom fields on the standard Individual DMO
optionD: Duplicate the standard Individual DMO and add the additional fields
explanation:
Creating custom fields on the standard Individual DMO is what the consultant should recommend. This keeps all individual profile data — standard and custom — on the same object, making it available for both segmentation (which operates on the Individual/Unified Individual) and identity resolution (which uses the Individual DMO).
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (custom DMO from scratch with all fields) — a separate custom DMO requires additional relationship mapping and is not used directly in identity resolution.
Option B (custom DMO with only the additional fields, mapped to Individual) — the same problem: the extra fields sit off the Individual DMO and are not available to identity resolution.
Option D (duplicate the standard Individual DMO) — not a supported pattern.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_map_custom_data_model_objects.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_required_data_mappings.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Northern Trail Outfitters wants to implement Data Cloud and has several use cases in mind. Which two use cases are considered a good fit for Data Cloud? (Choose 2).
optionA: To ingest and unify data from various sources to reconcile customer identity
optionB: To create and orchestrate cross-channel marketing messages
optionC: To use harmonized data to more accurately understand the customer and business impact
optionD: To eliminate the need for separate business intelligence and IT data management tools
explanation:
Ingesting and unifying data from various sources to reconcile customer identity, and using harmonized data to more accurately understand the customer and business impact, are the two good-fit use cases. Data Cloud's core capabilities are (A) ingesting data from multiple sources and unifying it through identity resolution to create a single customer view, and (C) using that harmonized unified data to generate insights about customers and business impact.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (create and orchestrate cross-channel marketing messages) — the domain of Marketing Cloud Journeys, not Data Cloud itself.
Option D (eliminate separate BI and IT data management tools) — not a Data Cloud value proposition; it complements those tools rather than replacing them.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_data_cloud.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Cumulus Financial offers both business and personal loans. Records in the Contact DLO can be useful for both groups since individual customers may have both business and personal loans. However, for legal reasons, the two groups must be kept separate. How should Cumulus Financial solve this business requirement?
optionA: Duplicate the Individual DMO
optionB: Duplicate the Contact DLO
optionC: Create two identity resolution rules in the same data space
optionD: Use two data spaces
explanation:
Using two data spaces is how Cumulus Financial should solve this. Data spaces provide complete logical separation of data within a single Data Cloud org — separate identity resolution, segmentation, and activation contexts. For legal requirements that mandate separation between business and personal loan customers, two data spaces is the correct architectural pattern. The same Contact DLO data can be referenced in both spaces as needed.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (duplicate the Individual DMO) — creates maintenance overhead without enforcing legal separation.
Option B (duplicate the Contact DLO) — the same: two copies of the data, but no boundary between the two groups.
Option C (two identity resolution rules in the same data space) — two rulesets in one data space share the same data pool and do not provide legal separation.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_data_spaces.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Which two common use cases can be addressed with Data Cloud? (Choose 2).
optionA: Understand and act upon customer data to drive more relevant experiences
optionB: Govern enterprise data lifecycle through a centralized set of policies and processes
optionC: Harmonize data from multiple sources with a standardized and extendable data model
optionD: Safeguard critical business data by serving as a centralized system for backup and disaster recovery
explanation:
Understanding and acting upon customer data to drive more relevant experiences, and harmonizing data from multiple sources with a standardized and extendable data model, are the two common Data Cloud use cases. Data Cloud's primary use cases are (A) creating unified customer profiles and activating them to deliver personalized, relevant experiences, and (C) harmonizing data from disparate sources into the standardized Customer 360 Data Model.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (govern the enterprise data lifecycle through centralized policies) — enterprise data governance is addressed by dedicated data governance platforms, not Data Cloud.
Option D (centralized system for backup and disaster recovery) — backup and disaster recovery are handled by dedicated backup solutions; Data Cloud is not one.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_data_cloud.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Northern Trail Outfitters wants to be able to calculate each customer's lifetime value (LTV) but also create breakdowns of the revenue sourced by website, mobile app, and retail channels. What should a consultant use to address this use case in Data Cloud?
optionA: Flow Orchestration
optionB: Nested segments
optionC: Metrics on metrics
optionD: Streaming data transform
explanation:
Metrics on metrics is what the consultant should use. Metrics on metrics (also known as multi-dimensional calculated insights) allow a consultant to first calculate a base metric (e.g., total revenue per channel) and then compute a higher-level metric on top of it (e.g., LTV as the sum of channel revenues). This is exactly what is needed — LTV overall plus channel-level breakdowns.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Flow Orchestration) — automates processes, not metric computation.
Option B (Nested segments) — filter populations; they do not compute revenue metrics.
Option D (Streaming data transform) — reshapes incoming data rather than computing aggregated insights.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_insights.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A marketing manager at Northern Trail Outfitters wants to improve marketing return on investment (ROI) by tapping into Insights from Data Cloud Segment Intelligence. Which permission set does a user need to set this up?
optionA: Data Cloud Data Aware Specialist
optionB: Data Cloud User
optionC: Cloud Marketing Manager
optionD: Data Cloud Admin
explanation:
Data Cloud Admin is the permission set a user needs to set up Segment Intelligence. Setting up Segment Intelligence is administrative work — connecting sources and configuring the feature — so it needs the permission set that grants all Data Cloud functionality, which this option calls Data Cloud Admin. Note the naming: as of 4 Sept 2025 the standard permission sets were renamed and this one is now Data Cloud Architect, described as giving access to all functionality within Data 360 including Data Cloud Setup, data mapping, data streams, identity resolution rulesets and insights.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Data Cloud Data Aware Specialist) — covers data mapping and modeling, not Data Cloud Setup and feature configuration.
Option B (Data Cloud User) — view-only.
Option C (Cloud Marketing Manager) — not a permission set name at all.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_userpermissions.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A user wants to be able to create a multi-dimensional metric to identify unified individual lifetime value (LTV). Which sequence of data model object (DMO) joins is necessary within the calculated insight to enable this calculation?
optionA: Unified Individual > Unified Link Individual > Sales Order
optionB: Unified Individual > Individual > Sales Order
optionC: Sales Order > Individual > Unified Individual
optionD: Sales Order > Unified Individual
explanation:
Unified Individual to Unified Link Individual to Sales Order is the necessary join sequence. To calculate LTV at the Unified Individual level, the calculated insight must join from Unified Individual through Unified Link Individual (the bridge object that maps unified profiles back to their source Individual records) and then to Sales Order (which holds transactional data). This is the correct join path in the Data Cloud unified data model.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (Unified Individual > Individual > Sales Order) — joining directly to Individual skips the unified link layer that ties source records to the unified profile.
Option C (Sales Order > Individual > Unified Individual) — an unconventional upward path that does not reflect the calculated insight join direction, and still omits Unified Link Individual.
Option D (Sales Order > Unified Individual) — skips Unified Link Individual entirely, so it is not a valid join path.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_identity_resolution.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_insights.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A consultant is planning the ingestion of a data stream that has profile information including a mobile phone number. To ensure that the phone number can be used for future SMS campaigns, they need to confirm the phone number field is in the proper E164 Phone Number format. However, the phone numbers in the file appear to be in varying formats. What is the most efficient way to guarantee that the various phone number formats are standardized?
optionA: Create a formula field to standardize the format
optionB: Edit and update the data in the source system prior to sending to Data Cloud
optionC: Assign the PhoneNumber field type when creating the data stream
optionD: Create a calculated insight after ingestion
explanation:
Creating a formula field to standardize the format is the most efficient way to guarantee E164. Assigning the phone data type does not standardize anything. Salesforce states it plainly: Data 360 doesn't validate the format of the phone number, the phone data type is modeled on the text data type, and any valid text value is accepted for ingestion into a phone field. Choosing that type only marks the field's intent. The same page points at the actual mechanism — formula functions that work with text values accept phone data type input, and you can convert the text output of those functions back into a phone data type — so a formula field applied at ingestion is what normalizes the varying formats into E164. The E164 requirement itself is real: it is the only format accepted for SMS sending, so the normalization has to happen somewhere.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (edit the data in the source system first) — works, but is the opposite of efficient and is often outside your control.
Option C (assign the PhoneNumber field type on the data stream) — the phone type is modeled on text, accepts any value and validates nothing, so it standardizes nothing.
Option D (calculated insight after ingestion) — computes metrics after ingestion rather than reshaping the stored field.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_data_types.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_considerations_formula_fields.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: Answer moved C->A. The keyed claim that assigning the PhoneNumber field type standardizes numbers into E164 is contradicted by the Data Types page, which says Data 360 does not validate phone format and accepts any text. The same page names formula functions as the supported way to transform the value.

question: What is the result of a segmentation criteria filtering on City | Is Equal To | 'San Jose'?
optionA: Cities containing 'San Jose', 'SAN JOSE', 'san jose', or 'San jose'
optionB: Cities only containing 'San Jose' or 'san jose'
optionC: Cities only containing 'San Jose'
optionD: Cities only containing 'San Jose' or 'SAN JOSE'
explanation:
Cities containing 'San Jose', 'SAN JOSE', 'san jose', or 'San jose' is the result. Salesforce documents segmentation queries as honoring exact matching on special characters and accents while not being case-sensitive. So 'Is Equal To' on City matches every casing of the entered value, and the remaining options each admit only a subset of those casings. Two boundaries are worth holding onto: case-insensitive is not a partial match, so 'San Jose, CA' is still excluded; and accents are matched exactly, which is why Salesforce's own example notes that a query for 'Canon City' finds 'canon city' but does not find 'Cañon City'.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B ('San Jose' or 'san jose' only) — too narrow; case-insensitive matching also admits 'SAN JOSE' and 'San jose'.
Option C ('San Jose' only) — treats the operator as case-sensitive, which it is not.
Option D ('San Jose' or 'SAN JOSE' only) — again a subset; every casing of the value matches.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_datatype_expression_operators.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: Q61 had options B and D identical and C repeating one string twice; deduped, and moved the answer to A, which is what the explanation already argued for.

question: Which information is provided in a .csv file when activating to Amazon S3?
optionA: An audit log showing the user who activated the segment and when it was activated
optionB: The activated data payload
optionC: The metadata regarding the segment definition
optionD: The manifest of origin sources within Data Cloud
explanation:
The activated data payload is what the .csv file provides. When Data Cloud activates to Amazon S3, the .csv file contains the activated data payload — the segment members and their selected attributes (contact points, related attributes, etc.). The .json file (not .csv) contains the metadata about the segment definition, activation ID, and schema.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (audit log of who activated the segment and when) — audit logs are available in Salesforce's audit trail, not in the S3 output.
Option C (metadata regarding the segment definition) — that lives in the .json manifest file, not the .csv.
Option D (manifest of origin sources) — also in the .json manifest file, not the .csv.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_find_segments_in_cloud_file_storage.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A customer has a Master Customer table from their CRM to ingest into Data Cloud. The table contains a name and primary email address, along with other personally identifiable information (PII). How should the fields be mapped to support identity resolution?
optionA: Create a new custom object with fields that directly match the incoming table
optionB: Map all fields to the Customer object
optionC: Map name to the Individual object and email address to the Contact Point Email object
optionD: Map all fields to the Individual object, adding a custom field for the email address
explanation:
Mapping name to the Individual object and email address to the Contact Point Email object is how the fields should be mapped. For identity resolution to work correctly, name fields must be mapped to the Individual DMO and email addresses must be mapped to the Contact Point Email DMO. This separation follows the Data Cloud standard data model — the Individual DMO holds identity attributes, while Contact Point objects hold contact details. Identity resolution matching rules reference these specific DMOs.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (new custom object matching the incoming table) — mapping everything to a custom object prevents the standard identity resolution rules from functioning.
Option B (map all fields to the Customer object) — there is no standard 'Customer' object in Data Cloud's data model.
Option D (all fields to Individual, with a custom email field) — a custom email field on Individual is invisible to the Contact Point Email match rules, so identity resolution cannot use it.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_required_data_mappings.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_contact_points.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Northern Trail Outfitters (NTO) creates a calculated insight to compute recency, frequency, monetary (RFM) scores on its unified individuals. NTO then creates a segment based on these scores that it activates to a Marketing Cloud activation target. Which two actions are required when configuring the activation? (Choose 2).
optionA: Add additional attributes
optionB: Choose a segment
optionC: Select contact points
optionD: Add the calculated insight in the activation
explanation:
Choosing a segment and selecting contact points are the two required actions when configuring the activation. When configuring any Marketing Cloud activation in Data Cloud, the activation must be linked to a segment that defines the population to activate (B), and Marketing Cloud requires a contact point (e.g., email address) to identify where to send the activation (C).
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (add additional attributes) — an optional enhancement, not a requirement.
Option D (add the calculated insight in the activation) — the calculated insight is already embedded in the segment's criteria; it does not need to be separately added to the activation.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_activation_for_a_segment.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_contact_points.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A Data Cloud consultant recently added a new data source and mapped some of the data to a new custom data model object (DMO) that they want to use for creating segments. However, they cannot view the newly created DMO when trying to create a new segment. What is the cause of this issue?
optionA: Data has not yet been ingested into the DMO
optionB: The new DMO is not of category Profile
optionC: The new DMO does not have a relationship to the individual DMO
optionD: Segmentation is only supported for the Individual and Unified Individual DMOs
explanation:
The new DMO not being of category Profile is the cause. In Data Cloud, only DMOs of category Profile are available as the primary segmentation object (the 'Segment On' object). If the newly created custom DMO was mapped with the Engagement or Other category, it will not appear in the segment builder as a segmentation target. The DMO must be assigned the Profile category for direct segmentation.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (data has not yet been ingested into the DMO) — lack of ingested data does not hide the DMO from the segment builder.
Option C (no relationship to the Individual DMO) — a relationship to Individual enables related-attribute segmentation but is not required for the DMO to appear.
Option D (segmentation only supports Individual and Unified Individual) — false; segmentation supports multiple Profile-category DMOs, not just Individual.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_category.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_segments.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Cumulus Financial created a segment called Multiple Investments that contains individuals who have invested in two or more mutual funds. The company plans to send an email to this segment regarding a new mutual fund offering, and wants to personalize the email content with information about each customer's current mutual fund investments. How should the Data Cloud consultant configure this activation?
optionA: Include Fund Type equal to 'Mutual Fund' as a related attribute. Configure an activation based on the new segment with no additional attributes
optionB: Choose the Multiple Investments segment, choose the Email contact point, add related attribute Fund Name, and add related attribute filter for Fund Type equal to 'Mutual Fund'
optionC: Choose the Multiple Investments segment, choose the Email contact point, and add related attribute Fund Type
optionD: Include Fund Name and Fund Type by default for post processing in the target system
explanation:
Choosing the Multiple Investments segment, choosing the Email contact point, adding the related attribute Fund Name and adding a related attribute filter for Fund Type equal to 'Mutual Fund' is how the activation should be configured. The activation must: (1) use the Multiple Investments segment; (2) select the Email contact point for delivery; (3) include Fund Name as a related attribute for personalization content; and (4) add a related attribute filter for Fund Type = 'Mutual Fund' to ensure only mutual fund investments (not other investment types) are included in the payload.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Fund Type filter as a related attribute, activation with no additional attributes) — configures a filter but no segment or contact point, and sends no Fund Name to personalize with.
Option C (segment, Email contact point, related attribute Fund Type) — omits the filter, so non-mutual-fund investments could be included, and carries Fund Type rather than the Fund Name needed for personalization.
Option D (Fund Name and Fund Type for post processing in the target system) — defers personalization logic to the target system, which is inefficient and is not a Data Cloud activation configuration.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_considerations_for_related_attributes.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_contact_points.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Which method should a consultant use when performing aggregations in windows of 15 minutes on data collected via the Interaction SDK or Mobile SDK?
optionA: Batch transform
optionB: Calculated insight
optionC: Streaming insight
optionD: Formula fields
explanation:
A streaming insight is the method to use. Streaming insights are designed for near-real-time aggregations over rolling time windows on streaming data — including data arriving via the Interaction SDK (web events) and Mobile SDK. A 15-minute aggregation window is a classic streaming insight use case.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Batch transform) — a scheduled batch operation, not suited for sub-hour rolling windows.
Option B (Calculated insight) — likewise batch-scheduled and not designed for 15-minute windows.
Option D (Formula fields) — operate at the field level during ingestion, not for aggregations over time windows.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_insights.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: How does Data Cloud ensure high availability and fault tolerance for customer data?
optionA: By distributing data across multiple regions and data centers
optionB: By using a data center with robust backups
optionC: By implementing automatic data recovery procedures
optionD: By limiting data access to essential personnel
explanation:
Distributing data across multiple regions and data centers is how Data Cloud ensures high availability and fault tolerance. Data Cloud is built on Salesforce's Hyperforce infrastructure, which distributes data across multiple geographic regions and data centers. This distributed architecture provides high availability (no single point of failure) and fault tolerance (data remains accessible even if one region experiences an outage).
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (a data center with robust backups) — a single data center with backups is a less resilient pattern than a distributed one.
Option C (automatic data recovery procedures) — a feature, but not the primary mechanism for high availability.
Option D (limiting data access to essential personnel) — a security measure, not a high availability strategy.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_data_cloud.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Which configuration supports separate Amazon S3 buckets for data ingestion and activation?
optionA: Dedicated S3 data sources in Data Cloud setup
optionB: Multiple S3 connectors in Data Cloud setup
optionC: Dedicated S3 data sources in activation setup
optionD: Separate user credentials for data stream and activation target
explanation:
Dedicated S3 data sources in Data Cloud setup is the configuration that supports separate buckets for ingestion and activation. Data Cloud supports configuring separate Amazon S3 connections — one configured as the ingestion data source (in Data Cloud Setup > Connected Apps / Data Streams) and another as the activation target. Using dedicated S3 data sources in Data Cloud setup for ingestion, and a separate S3 bucket configured in the activation target settings, allows complete separation of ingestion and activation buckets.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (multiple S3 connectors in Data Cloud setup) — describes the underlying mechanism loosely, but "dedicated S3 data sources in Data Cloud setup" is the specific correct phrasing the item is looking for.
Option C (dedicated S3 data sources in activation setup) — data sources for ingestion are configured in Data Cloud Setup, not in activation setup; the activation side is an activation target.
Option D (separate user credentials for data stream and activation target) — separate credentials alone do not enforce bucket separation.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_data_ingestion.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_create_cloud_file_storage_activation_target.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A consultant is ingesting a list of employees from their human resources database that they want to segment on. Which data stream category should the consultant choose when ingesting this data?
optionA: Profile Data
optionB: Contact Data
optionC: Other Data
optionD: Engagement Data
explanation:
Profile Data is the data stream category to choose. Profile is the category for data that describes who someone is, and Salesforce's Category page names this case directly: choose Profile if your dataset is a list of individuals with identifiers, a list of businesses or accounts, or a list of employees or any other population that you want to segment on. Employee records from an HR system are exactly that. Worth remembering when you pick: the category can't be changed after the data stream is saved.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (Contact Data) — not a Data Cloud data stream category.
Option C (Other Data) — for reference data that is neither profile nor engagement, not a population to segment on.
Option D (Engagement Data) — for time-series event data, and requires an event date-time field to be nominated at setup; an employee list has none.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_category.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A customer has multiple team members who create segment audiences that work in different time zones. One team member works at the home office in the Pacific time zone, that matches the org Time Zone setting. Another team member works remotely in the Eastern time zone. Which user will see their home time zone in the segment and activation schedule areas?
optionA: The team member in the Pacific time zone
optionB: The team member in the Eastern time zone
optionC: Neither team member; Data Cloud shows all schedules in GMT
optionD: Both team members; Data Cloud adjusts the segment and activation schedules to the time zone of the logged-in user
explanation:
Both team members see their home time zone, because Data Cloud adjusts the segment and activation schedules to the time zone of the logged-in user. Segment and activation schedule fields display the publish schedule start date and time in the logged-in user's time zone, so each team member sees their own local time. The org time zone is not irrelevant, though — it still governs other segmentation behaviour, notably the date-based operators such as Last Number Of Days. Two practical consequences: your org sets the publish time zone on the initial segment save, and a later change to the org's time zone is not picked up by existing segments unless you resave them.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (the Pacific team member only) — matching the org time zone is not what decides the display; the logged-in user's time zone is, for everyone.
Option B (the Eastern team member only) — likewise; the remote user is not singled out, both see local time.
Option C (neither; all schedules shown in GMT) — schedules are not displayed in GMT; they are converted to each user's time zone.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_time_zones.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_datatype_expression_operators.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: How does identity resolution select attributes for unified individuals when there is conflicting information in the data model?
optionA: Creates additional contact points
optionB: Leverages reconciliation rules
optionC: Creates additional rulesets
optionD: Leverages match rules
explanation:
Leveraging reconciliation rules is how identity resolution selects attributes when information conflicts. When multiple source records are merged into a unified individual and those records have conflicting values for the same attribute (e.g., different addresses), identity resolution uses reconciliation rules to determine which value to use on the unified profile. Reconciliation rules can be set to Last Updated, Most Occurring, Source Priority, or other strategies.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (creates additional contact points) — contact points are a separate construct; conflicting attribute values are not resolved by adding more of them.
Option C (creates additional rulesets) — rulesets define match and reconciliation configuration; identity resolution does not spawn new ones to resolve conflicts.
Option D (leverages match rules) — match rules determine whether two records represent the same individual; they do not select attribute values.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_reconciliation_rules.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Which statement is true related to batch ingestions from Salesforce CRM?
optionA: When a column is added or removed, the CRM connector performs a full refresh
optionB: The CRM connector performs an incremental refresh when 600K or more deletion records are detected
optionC: The CRM connector's synchronization times can be customized to up to 15-minute intervals
optionD: CRM data cannot be manually refreshed and must wait for the next scheduled synchronization
explanation:
A full refresh being performed by the CRM connector when a column is added or removed is the true statement. When a schema change occurs on a CRM object — such as adding or removing a field that is part of the data stream — the CRM Connector automatically triggers a full refresh to ensure the data lake is consistent with the new schema. Incremental refreshes handle row-level changes; schema changes require a full reload.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (incremental refresh when 600K or more deletions are detected) — the 600K deletion threshold triggers a full refresh for deletions, not an incremental one, so the statement has the refresh type backwards.
Option C (synchronization times customizable to 15-minute intervals) — false; synchronization times are not customizable by the user.
Option D (CRM data cannot be manually refreshed) — false; CRM data can be manually refreshed.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_data_stream_edit_settings.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_crm_store_deleted_data_stream_records.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Which two steps should a consultant take if a successfully configured Amazon S3 data stream fails to refresh with a 'NO FILE FOUND' error message? (Choose 2).
optionA: Check if correct permissions are configured for the Data Cloud user
optionB: Check if the Amazon S3 data source is enabled in Data Cloud Setup
optionC: Check if the file exists in the specified bucket location
optionD: Check if correct permissions are configured for the S3 user
explanation:
Checking that correct permissions are configured for the Data Cloud user, and checking that the file exists in the specified bucket location, are the two steps to take. A 'NO FILE FOUND' error on an S3 data stream refresh means Data Cloud attempted to read the file and either couldn't find it or couldn't access it. If permissions for the Data Cloud user or connected credentials are misconfigured, Data Cloud cannot read the bucket, which can manifest as a not-found error (A); and if the upstream process didn't deliver the file to the configured bucket path, there is nothing to ingest (C).
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (check the S3 data source is enabled in Data Cloud Setup) — a disabled data source would prevent configuration at all, not cause a refresh failure on a successfully configured stream.
Option D (check permissions for the S3 user) — overlaps with option A, but A is the more precise check within Data Cloud's configuration.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_data_streams.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_data_ingestion.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Cumulus Financial is currently using Data Cloud and ingesting transactional data from its backend system via an S3 Connector in upsert mode. During the initial setup six months ago, the company created a formula field in Data Cloud to create a custom classification. It now needs to update this formula to account for more classifications. What should the consultant keep in mind with regard to formula field updates when using the S3 Connector?
optionA: Data Cloud will update the formula for all records at the next incremental upsert refresh
optionB: Data Cloud does not support formula field updates for data streams of type upsert
optionC: Data Cloud will initiate a full refresh of data from S3 and will update the formula on all records
optionD: Data Cloud will only update the formula on a go-forward basis for new records
explanation:
Data Cloud initiating a full refresh of data from S3 and updating the formula on all records is what the consultant should keep in mind. When a formula field is updated on a data stream using the S3 Connector in upsert mode, Data Cloud triggers a full refresh of the data stream — re-ingesting all records from S3 and applying the updated formula to every record. This ensures historical data reflects the new formula logic.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (update at the next incremental upsert refresh) — an incremental refresh would only process new or changed records, missing historical ones.
Option B (formula updates not supported for upsert streams) — false; formula updates are supported for upsert streams.
Option D (update only on a go-forward basis for new records) — would leave historical records with stale formula values, which is not what happens.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_full_replace.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_considerations_formula_fields.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: An organization wants to enable users with the ability to identify and select text attributes from a picklist of options. Which Data Cloud feature should help with this use case?
optionA: Value suggestion
optionB: Data harmonization
optionC: Transformation formulas
optionD: Global picklists
explanation:
Value suggestion is the Data Cloud feature for this use case. Value suggestion presents users with a dropdown of available attribute values when building segment criteria. When enabled on a DMO attribute, it indexes the distinct values and surfaces them as selectable options in the segment builder, making it easy to pick from known values rather than typing them manually.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (Data harmonization) — a broader concept about mapping sources into the data model, not a picker of attribute values.
Option C (Transformation formulas) — for field derivation during ingestion, not for selecting values at segmentation time.
Option D (Global picklists) — a Salesforce CRM feature, not native to Data Cloud segmentation.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_suggested_values_in_segments.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Northern Trail Outfitters (NTO) wants to send a promotional campaign for customers that have purchased within the past 6 months. The consultant created a segment to meet this requirement. Now, NTO brings an additional requirement to suppress customers who have made purchases within the last week. What should the consultant use to remove the recent customers?
optionA: Batch transforms
optionB: Segmentation exclude rules
optionC: Related attributes
optionD: Streaming insight
explanation:
Segmentation exclude rules are what the consultant should use to remove the recent customers. Segmentation exclude rules (exclusion containers) allow a consultant to add an exclusion condition to an existing segment — in this case, excluding individuals who made a purchase within the last week. This is cleaner than modifying the main segment criteria and clearly communicates the suppression intent.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Batch transforms) — reshape data; they do not filter segment membership.
Option C (Related attributes) — add data to an activation payload; they do not exclude segment members.
Option D (Streaming insight) — enables real-time event actions, not segment suppression.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_segments.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.c360_a_container_basics.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: During a privacy law discussion with a customer, the customer indicates they need to honor requests for the right to be forgotten. The consultant determines that Consent API will solve this business need. Which two considerations should the consultant inform the customer about? (Choose 2).
optionA: Data deletion requests are reprocessed at 30, 60, and 90 days
optionB: Data deletion requests are processed within 1 hour
optionC: Data deletion requests are submitted for Individual profiles
optionD: Data deletion requests submitted to Data Cloud are passed to all connected Salesforce clouds
explanation:
Data deletion requests being reprocessed at 30, 60, and 90 days, and being submitted for Individual profiles, are the two considerations to inform the customer about. Deletion requests are reprocessed at 30, 60, and 90 days, so that any data for the individual that arrived after the original request is also removed and full deletion can be verified (A), and requests are submitted against Individual profiles, which is the entity Data Cloud deletes by (C).
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (processed within 1 hour) — the one-hour processing claim is not the documented commitment.
Option D (passed to all connected Salesforce clouds) — inverts the actual behaviour and is the trap here: a deletion request submitted to Data Cloud is not propagated outward, and Salesforce is explicit that you must submit deletion requests separately in every connected system and Salesforce cloud.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_data_deletion_request.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: Q78 C,D->A,C. Deletion requests are reprocessed at 30/60/90 days, and they are NOT propagated to connected clouds — you must submit separately.

question: Which data stream category type should be assigned in order to use the dataset for date and time-based operations in segmentation and calculated insights?
optionA: Individual
optionB: Engagement
optionC: Sales Order
optionD: Profile
explanation:
Engagement is the data stream category to assign for date and time-based operations. The Engagement category is required for data streams that will be used in date and time-based operations — such as 'events in the last 7 days' or time-window aggregations in calculated insights and streaming insights. Engagement-type DMOs have an Event Time field that enables temporal filtering and aggregation.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Individual) — a specific DMO, not a data stream category type.
Option C (Sales Order) — likewise a specific DMO, not a category.
Option D (Profile) — for static identity attributes; Profile-category DMOs do not support the same time-based operations.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_category.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A consultant is building a segment to announce a new product launch for customers that have previously purchased black pants. How should the consultant place attributes for product color and product type from the Order Product object to meet this criteria?
optionA: Place the attribute for product color in one container and the attribute for product type in another container
optionB: Place an attribute for the 'black' calculated insight to dynamically apply
optionC: Place the attributes for product and product type as direct attributes
optionD: Place the attributes for product color and product type in a single container
explanation:
Placing the attributes for product color and product type in a single container is how the consultant should build this. To find customers who purchased black pants — meaning a single product that is both black AND pants — both attributes must be evaluated against the same product record. Placing both Product Color = Black and Product Type = Pants in a single container ensures they are applied as AND conditions on the same Order Product row.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (product color in one container, product type in another) — evaluates them independently across any product in any order; a customer who bought black shoes and white pants would incorrectly qualify.
Option B (an attribute for the 'black' calculated insight) — there is no such calculated insight, and an insight is not how a same-row condition is expressed on the canvas.
Option C (product and product type as direct attributes) — direct attributes only work for attributes on the primary segmented DMO, not on the related Order Product object.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.c360_a_container_basics.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A segment fails to refresh with the error 'Segment references too many data lake objects (DLOS)'. Which two troubleshooting tips should help remedy this issue? (Choose 2).
optionA: Split the segment into smaller segments
optionB: Use calculated insights in order to reduce the complexity of the segmentation query
optionC: Refine segmentation criteria to limit up to five custom data model objects (DMOs)
optionD: Space out the segment schedules to reduce DLO load
explanation:
Splitting the segment into smaller segments, and using calculated insights to reduce the complexity of the segmentation query, are the two troubleshooting tips. When a segment exceeds the DLO reference limit, splitting it into smaller, more focused segments reduces the number of DLOs each individual segment references (A), and pre-computing complex multi-DLO logic in a Calculated Insight and referencing that insight in the segment dramatically reduces the number of DLOs the segment query must join at runtime (B).
Why the other options are wrong:
Option C (limit to five custom DMOs) — a good practice but not a specific documented remedy for this error.
Option D (space out the segment schedules) — addresses concurrency, not DLO count.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_segmentation_troubleshooting.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: The Data Cloud admin at Northern Trail Outfitters (NTO) wants to be proactively and immediately informed via Slack and email if any of the data streams fail for any reason. If this happens, a case should also be triggered as part of NTO's existing support and triage process, and reflected in its global monitoring dashboard. What should a consultant recommend for these requirements?
optionA: Data actions
optionB: Data Cloud Query Editor
optionC: Salesforce flows
optionD: Salesforce reports and dashboards
explanation:
Salesforce flows are what the consultant should recommend. Salesforce Flows can monitor Data Cloud data stream failure events and orchestrate multi-step notifications — sending a Slack message, sending an email, creating a Case record, and updating a dashboard — all from a single automation. Flows are the appropriate tool for orchestrating cross-system notifications and record creation based on Data Cloud events.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Data actions) — trigger from insight thresholds and data changes, not from data stream failures, and cannot create a Case on their own.
Option B (Data Cloud Query Editor) — a manual querying tool with no automation.
Option D (Salesforce reports and dashboards) — display data but do not trigger proactive notifications.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_data_cloud.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: (Variant) A user is not seeing suggested values from newly-modeled data when building a segment. What is causing this issue?
optionA: Value suggestion is still processing and will be available soon
optionB: Value suggestion requires Data Aware Specialist permissions at a minimum
optionC: Value suggestion can only work on direct attributes and not related attributes
optionD: Value suggestion will only return results for the first 50 values of a specific attribute
explanation:
Value suggestion still processing and becoming available soon is what is causing the issue. Value suggestions are computed asynchronously after data is modeled, and Salesforce states that it can take up to 24 hours for suggested values to appear — so a user who has just modeled new data is most likely still waiting. Value suggestions are enabled per Text field from the DMO record home, for up to 500 attributes across the org, and are retained for 30 days.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (requires Data Aware Specialist permissions) — permissions govern access rather than suggestion availability.
Option C (direct attributes only, not related attributes) — narrower than stated: for a DMO in the Other category, value suggestion works on one-to-one and many-to-one relationships and is unavailable on one-to-many. It is not the cause here.
Option D (only the first 50 values of an attribute) — there is no 50-value cap; the documented behaviour is that an attribute with more than 1,000 values shows the 1,000 most frequently occurring values alphabetically.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_suggested_values_in_segments.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A retail customer wants to bring customer data from different sources and wants to take advantage of identity resolution so that it can be used in segmentation. On which entity should this be segmented for activation membership?
optionA: Subscriber
optionB: Unified Individual
optionC: Unified Contact
optionD: Individual
explanation:
The Unified Individual is the entity to segment on for activation membership. When identity resolution is used, multiple source Individual records are merged into a Unified Individual — the single consolidated customer profile. Segmentation and activation membership should target the Unified Individual to ensure each customer is represented once, with the best available data from all sources.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Subscriber) — not a standard Data Cloud segmentation entity.
Option C (Unified Contact) — not a standard Data Cloud segmentation entity either.
Option D (Individual) — would count each source record separately, potentially activating the same person multiple times.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_activation_for_a_segment.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Cumulus Financial is experiencing delays in publishing multiple segments simultaneously. The company wants to avoid reducing the frequency at which segments are published, while retaining the same segments in place today. Which action should a consultant take to alleviate this issue?
optionA: Enable rapid segment publishing to all segments to reduce generation time
optionB: Reduce the number of segments being published
optionC: Increase the Data Cloud segmentation concurrency limit
optionD: Adjust the publish schedule start time of each segment to prevent overlapping processes
explanation:
Increasing the Data Cloud segmentation concurrency limit is the keyed action. Raising the limit is a legitimate lever and is kept as the answer: Salesforce says outright that because Data 360 is built to scale, some limits can be adjusted to meet your business needs by working with your account executive, and concurrent publishing is a real constraint — the limits page caps rapid concurrent publishes at 20. Be aware, though, that Salesforce's own remedy for the error "Too many segments are trying to publish at the same time" is to wait for some segments to finish and to change the publish schedule for some of your segments. Staggering publish start times is therefore the documented first response, and it does not conflict with this scenario's constraints — offsetting when each segment starts changes neither the set of segments nor how often each one runs. This item therefore has two defensible options.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (enable rapid segment publishing on all segments) — rapid publish is a per-segment publishing mode rather than a fix for queue contention.
Option B (reduce the number of segments being published) — the option genuinely ruled out by the requirements, which keep the same segments in place.
Option D (adjust the publish schedule start time of each segment) — not wrong in practice: it is Salesforce's documented remedy for simultaneous publishes and respects both constraints. It is excluded only because the item keys the concurrency limit.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_segmentation_troubleshooting.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_limits_and_guidelines.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: Answer stands, but the old explanation dismissed option D on a false premise — it claimed staggering schedules compromises the requirement to keep all segments at the same frequency, which it does not. Salesforce's Troubleshoot Segment Errors page names changing the publish schedule as the remedy for simultaneous publishes, so this item has two defensible options.

question: A consultant is setting up Data Cloud for a multi-brand organization and is using data spaces to segregate its data for various brands. While starting the mapping of a data stream, the consultant notices that they cannot map the object for one of the brands. What should the consultant do to make the object available for a new data space?
optionA: Create a new data stream and map the second data stream to the data space
optionB: Copy data from the default data space to a new DMO using the Data Copy feature and link this DMO to the new data space
optionC: Create a batch transform to split data between different data spaces
optionD: Navigate to the Data Space tab and select the object to be included in the new data space
explanation:
Navigating to the Data Space tab and selecting the object to include in the new data space is what the consultant should do. DMOs and DLOs must be explicitly added to a data space before they can be used for mapping within that space. The consultant should navigate to the Data Space configuration and add the relevant object to the target data space. This makes it available for data stream mapping in that space.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (create a new data stream and map it to the data space) — unnecessary; the object already exists and only needs to be included in the data space.
Option B (Data Copy into a new DMO linked to the new data space) — also unnecessary duplication; data space membership is a configuration setting, not a copy of the data.
Option C (batch transform to split data between data spaces) — batch transforms do not control data space membership.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_data_spaces.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A consultant is working in a customer's Data Cloud org and is asked to delete the existing identity resolution ruleset. Which two impacts should the consultant communicate as a result of this action? (Choose 2).
optionA: All individual data will be removed
optionB: Unified customer data associated with this ruleset will be removed
optionC: Dependencies on data model objects will be removed
optionD: All source profile data will be removed
explanation:
Unified customer data associated with the ruleset being removed, and dependencies on data model objects being removed, are the two impacts to communicate. Salesforce states the consequences in one sentence: deleting a ruleset permanently removes all unified customer data, eliminates dependencies on data model objects, stops all processing of the ruleset, and deletes the history of previous runs. That is options B and C. Two practical points: deletion takes up to 24 hours to complete and previous unification data can't be recovered afterwards, so where the goal is to change matching behaviour while keeping the same ruleset name and ID, update the match or reconciliation rules instead of deleting.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (all individual data will be removed) — source profile data is untouched; the ingested records remain in the data lake and can be unified again by a new ruleset.
Option D (all source profile data will be removed) — the same: the loss is of the unified output rather than the raw data.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_identity_resolution_deletion.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A consultant is discussing the benefits of Data Cloud with a customer that has multiple disjointed data sources. Which two functional areas should the consultant highlight in relation to managing customer data? (Choose 2).
optionA: Data Harmonization
optionB: Unified Profiles
optionC: Master Data Management
optionD: Data Marketplace
explanation:
Data Harmonization and Unified Profiles are the two functional areas to highlight. For a customer with multiple disjointed data sources, the two most relevant Data Cloud functional areas are Data Harmonization (A) — mapping disparate source data into a standardized data model so it can be used consistently — and Unified Profiles (B) — merging harmonized data across sources through identity resolution to create a single 360-degree customer view.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option C (Master Data Management) — a related discipline but not a specific Data Cloud capability.
Option D (Data Marketplace) — for acquiring third-party data, not managing existing sources.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_data_cloud.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A consultant is setting up a data stream with transactional data. Which field type should the consultant choose to ensure that leading zeros in the purchase order number are preserved?
optionA: Text
optionB: Number
optionC: Decimal
optionD: Serial
explanation:
Text is the field type that preserves leading zeros. Text fields store values as alphanumeric strings exactly as provided — including leading zeros. For a purchase order number like '00123', only a Text field preserves the '00' prefix. This is a key data modeling decision when ingesting identifiers that look numeric but must retain their full string representation.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (Number) — stores the value as a numeric type and strips leading zeros when parsing.
Option C (Decimal) — likewise numeric; '00123' becomes 123.
Option D (Serial) — a numeric type as well, so the leading zeros are lost.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_data_types.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A retailer wants to unify profiles using Loyalty ID which is different than the unique ID of their customers. Which object should the consultant use in identity resolution to perform exact match rules on the Loyalty ID?
optionA: Party Identification object
optionB: Loyalty Identification object
optionC: Individual object
optionD: Contact Identification object
explanation:
The Party Identification object is the object to use for exact match rules on the Loyalty ID. The Party Identification DMO is the standard Data Cloud object for storing alternative or secondary identifiers for an individual — such as loyalty IDs, passport numbers, or any custom identifier that is distinct from the system primary key. By mapping the Loyalty ID to the Party Identification object and creating an exact match rule on that field, the consultant enables identity resolution to unify profiles based on shared loyalty IDs.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (Loyalty Identification object) — there is no standard Loyalty Identification object in Data Cloud.
Option C (Individual object) — holds core identity attributes, not secondary IDs.
Option D (Contact Identification object) — there is no standard Contact Identification object in Data Cloud.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_match_rules.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_required_data_mappings.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A Data Cloud Consultant is in the process of setting up data streams for a new service-based data source. When ingesting Case data, which field is recommended to be associated with the Event Time field?
optionA: Last Modified Date
optionB: Resolution Date
optionC: Escalation Date
optionD: Creation Date
explanation:
Creation Date is the field recommended for the Event Time field when ingesting Case data. The Event Time field in Data Cloud represents when the event or record originated — for Case data, this is the Creation Date (the moment the case was opened). Event Time is used for time-based filtering in streaming insights and segmentation. Creation Date is the most semantically accurate choice for when the case 'happened.'
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Last Modified Date) — represents when the case was last changed, not when it occurred.
Option B (Resolution Date) — a downstream state, not the originating event time.
Option C (Escalation Date) — also a downstream state, and empty for cases that were never escalated.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_category.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A consultant has an activation that is set to publish every 12 hours, but has discovered that updates to the data prior to activation are delayed by up to 24 hours. Which two areas should a consultant review to troubleshoot this issue? (Choose 2).
optionA: Review data transformations to ensure they're run after calculated insights
optionB: Review calculated insights to make sure they're run before segments are refreshed
optionC: Review segments to ensure they're refreshed after the data is ingested
optionD: Review calculated insights to make sure they're run after the segments are refreshed
explanation:
Reviewing calculated insights to make sure they run before segments are refreshed, and reviewing segments to ensure they are refreshed after the data is ingested, are the two areas to review. A 24-hour delay in data reaching activation suggests a pipeline sequencing issue. Calculated insights must run before segments are refreshed — if insights run after segment refresh, the segment uses stale insight data (B); and segments must be refreshed after data ingestion completes — if the segment refresh runs before new data is ingested, it operates on the previous day's data (C). These two sequencing gaps together can create up to 24-hour delays.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (data transformations run after calculated insights) — the wrong order; transformations feed the data that calculated insights compute on, so they run before.
Option D (calculated insights run after segments are refreshed) — this is the problem scenario, not the fix.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_insights.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_publish_segment.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A consultant needs to minimize the difference between a Data Cloud segment population and Marketing Cloud data extension count to determine the true size of segments for campaign planning. What should the consultant recommend to filter the segments by to accomplish this?
optionA: Marketing Cloud Journeys
optionB: Business units
optionC: User preferences for marketing outreach
optionD: Geographical divisions
explanation:
Business units are what the consultant should recommend filtering the segments by. The most common cause of a population difference between a Data Cloud segment and the resulting Marketing Cloud data extension count is that the segment contains unified individuals who belong to multiple Marketing Cloud business units. Filtering the segment by business unit ensures that only individuals with contact points in the relevant business unit are activated, aligning the counts.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Marketing Cloud Journeys) — journeys affect who enters a campaign flow, not base segment size.
Option C (user preferences for marketing outreach) — a criterion that could be applied, but not the cause of this specific population mismatch.
Option D (geographical divisions) — likewise a possible filter, but not the standard answer to a segment-versus-data-extension count gap.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_segments.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_activation_for_a_segment.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A customer has a calculated insight about lifetime value. What does the consultant need to be aware of if the calculated insight needs to be modified?
optionA: New dimensions can be added
optionB: Existing dimensions can be removed
optionC: Existing measures can be removed
optionD: New measures can be added
explanation:
New dimensions can be added is the keyed answer. The safe reading is that a calculated insight can be extended but not narrowed: new dimensions can be added to an existing insight, while removing an existing dimension or an existing measure is not available, because downstream segments and activations may already depend on them. Treat this item's option set with care, though — adding a new measure (D) is also possible, so A is not uniquely correct as printed, and the distinction the question is reaching for is between adding and removing rather than between dimensions and measures. If you are planning an insight that others will build on, the rule worth carrying is the one this item half-expresses: design the dimensions and measures you need up front, because you can extend the insight later but you cannot take pieces away.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (existing dimensions can be removed) — removal is not available; downstream segments and activations may depend on the dimension.
Option C (existing measures can be removed) — the same: measures cannot be taken away once the insight exists.
Option D (new measures can be added) — actually true, which is why this item is defective; it is excluded only because the item keys A.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_insights.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_calculated_insights_in_segments.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Cumulus Financial wants to create a segment of individuals based on transaction history data. This data has been mapped in the data model and is accessible via multiple container paths for segmentation. What happens if the optimal container path for this use case is not selected?
optionA: Alternate container paths will be suggested before the segment is published
optionB: The resulting segment may be smaller or larger than expected
optionC: Data Cloud segmentation will automatically select the optimal container path
optionD: The resulting segment will not be generated
explanation:
The resulting segment being smaller or larger than expected is what happens when the optimal container path is not selected. Container paths in segmentation determine how DMOs are joined when evaluating criteria. Different paths through the data model can yield different join cardinalities — the same logical criteria applied via different paths can produce different population counts (either over-counting or under-counting). Selecting the wrong path may result in a segment that is larger than expected (due to fan-out from a one-to-many join) or smaller (if the path excludes records).
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (alternate container paths suggested before publishing) — Data Cloud does not suggest alternative paths.
Option C (Data Cloud automatically selects the optimal path) — it does not; the path chosen on the canvas is the path used.
Option D (the segment will not be generated) — false; the segment still generates, just with potentially incorrect membership.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.c360_a_container_basics.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_considerations_for_related_attributes.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Which two requirements must be met for a calculated insight to appear in the segmentation canvas? (Choose 2).
optionA: The metrics of the calculated insights must only contain numeric values
optionB: The primary key of the segmented table must be a metric in the calculated insight
optionC: The calculated insight must contain a dimension including the Individual or Unified Individual Id
optionD: The primary key of the segmented table must be a dimension in the calculated insight
explanation:
A dimension including the Individual or Unified Individual Id, and the primary key of the segmented table as a dimension in the calculated insight, are the two requirements. The insight must include a dimension that contains the Individual Id or Unified Individual Id — this links the insight back to the individual being segmented (C); and the primary key of the table being segmented must appear as a dimension in the calculated insight — this allows Data Cloud to join the insight to the segmented entity (D).
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (metrics must only contain numeric values) — generally true of metrics, but not the requirement for appearance in the canvas.
Option B (primary key of the segmented table as a metric) — incorrect; the primary key must be a dimension, not a metric.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_calculated_insights_in_segments.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A company wants to include certain personalized fields in an email by including related attributes during the activation in Data Cloud. It notices that some values, such as purchased product names, do not have consistent casing in Marketing Cloud Engagement. The company wants to normalize all names to proper case and replace any null values with a default value. How should a consultant fulfill this requirement within Data Cloud?
optionA: Create a streaming insight with a data action
optionB: Use formula fields when ingesting at the data stream level
optionC: Create one batch data transform per data stream
optionD: Create one batch data transform that creates a new DLO
explanation:
Creating one batch data transform that creates a new DLO is how the consultant should fulfill this requirement. A batch data transform that creates a new DLO is the correct approach for normalizing casing and replacing nulls across a dataset. The transform can apply PROPER() case functions and COALESCE/IFNULL logic across all records, writing the cleaned data to a new DLO that is then mapped and activated.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (streaming insight with a data action) — for real-time event triggers, not batch data cleansing.
Option B (formula fields at the data stream level) — work on individual records at ingest time but are less suited for cross-record normalization and null replacement at scale.
Option C (one batch data transform per data stream) — less efficient than a single transform that creates one consolidated DLO.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_batch_transform_formula.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Where is value suggestion for attributes in segmentation enabled when creating the DMO?
optionA: Data Mapping
optionB: Data Transformation
optionC: Segment Setup
optionD: Data Stream Setup
explanation:
Data Mapping is where value suggestion is enabled when creating the DMO. Data Mapping is the right stage, because value suggestion is a property of the data model object rather than of any segment. Salesforce's page on the feature says you can enable value suggestions for DMO fields whose data type is Text, and that you enable or deactivate the feature in the DMO record home — the data-modeling area where the DMO is created and mapped — with a ceiling of 500 attributes across the org. The segment canvas is where the suggestions are consumed rather than switched on: you drag the attribute in and start typing in the Value field, and it can take up to 24 hours after modeling for values to appear. Note that no option names the DMO record home exactly, which is this item's wording weakness; Data Mapping is the option that describes the correct stage.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (Data Transformation) — acts on the data lake object before anything reaches the model; value suggestion is a DMO property.
Option C (Segment Setup) — the segment canvas is where suggestions are used, not where they are switched on.
Option D (Data Stream Setup) — also acts on the data lake object, upstream of the DMO where the feature lives.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_suggested_values_in_segments.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: What should an organization use to stream inventory levels from an inventory management system into Data Cloud in a fast and scalable, near-real-time way?
optionA: Cloud Storage Connector
optionB: Commerce Cloud Connector
optionC: Ingestion API
optionD: Marketing Cloud Personalization Connector
explanation:
The Ingestion API is what the organization should use. The Ingestion API is Data Cloud's mechanism for streaming data from external systems in near-real-time. It accepts JSON payloads via REST API calls, making it ideal for an inventory management system to push level changes as they occur — fast, scalable, and programmable.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Cloud Storage Connector) — for batch file-based ingestion, not real-time streaming.
Option B (Commerce Cloud Connector) — specific to Salesforce B2C/B2B Commerce, not an external inventory system.
Option D (Marketing Cloud Personalization Connector) — for behavioral personalization data, not inventory.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_data_ingestion.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Cumulus Financial wants its service agents to view a display of all cases associated with a Unified Individual on a contact record. Which two features should a consultant consider for this use case? (Choose 2).
optionA: Data Action
optionB: Profile API
optionC: Lightning Web Components
optionD: Query APL
explanation:
The Profile API and Lightning Web Components are the two features to consider. To surface unified Data Cloud profile data (including associated cases) directly on a Salesforce Contact record for service agents, the Profile API allows querying unified individual data from Data Cloud programmatically (B), and Lightning Web Components can be built to call the Profile API and display the results embedded on the Contact record page (C).
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Data Action) — data actions trigger events from Data Cloud outward; they do not display data inward on a record page.
Option D (Query APL) — the Query API is Data Cloud's query interface for analytics, not for embedding real-time data in the Salesforce UI.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_data_cloud.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_profile_explorer.htm&language=en_US&type=5
